statement: For the parabola $y^{2}=4ax$, show that the tangent at the point $(at^{2},2at)$ has equation $ty=x+at^{2}$, and find where this tangent meets the $x$-axis.
solution: The point $(at^{2},2at)$ lies on $y^{2}=4ax$ since $(2at)^{2}=4a\cdot at^{2}$. The tangent has gradient $\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{dy/dt}{dx/dt}=\frac{2a}{2at}=\frac{1}{t}$, so its equation is $y-2at=\frac{1}{t}(x-at^{2})$, i.e. $ty=x+at^{2}$. Setting $y=0$ gives $x=-at^{2}$, so the tangent meets the $x$-axis at $(-at^{2},0)$.
hints: Differentiate parametrically to find the gradient dy/dx.
Use the point-slope form of the tangent.
Set y=0 to find the x-intercept.
